subject: ela
cluster: Range of reading and level of text complexity

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Ants are very strong for their size. An ant can carry up to 50 times its own body weight. Ants live and work in large colonies. Each ant has a specific job, such as gathering food, protecting the colony, or caring for young ants.

What is this passage mostly about?

choices.label: A
choices.text: How to find ant colonies in the wild

choices.label: B
choices.text: The strength and social organization of ants

choices.label: C
choices.text: How ants build their underground homes

choices.label: D
choices.text: The difference between ants and termites

items.explanation: The passage covers two main points: ants' strength (carrying 50 times their weight) and how ants are organized in colonies with specific jobs. Option B captures both main points.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

How to Make a Paper Airplane:
Step 1: Start with a flat sheet of paper.
Step 2: Fold the paper in half lengthwise and then unfold it.
Step 3: Fold the top two corners down to the center crease.
Step 4: Fold the angled edges to the center again.
Step 5: Fold the plane in half along the center crease and fold the wings down.

What is the purpose of this text?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To compare paper airplanes to real airplanes

choices.label: B
choices.text: To tell the history of paper folding

choices.label: C
choices.text: To give step-by-step instructions for making something

choices.label: D
choices.text: To explain how real airplanes fly

items.explanation: The text gives numbered, sequential steps for making a paper airplane. This is a how-to or procedural text whose purpose is to provide instructions.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Jackie Robinson was born in Georgia in 1919. He excelled at four sports in college. In 1947, he became the first Black player in Major League Baseball. He faced terrible discrimination but kept playing. His courage and skill helped break the color barrier in professional sports.

What is one key detail that supports the main idea that Jackie Robinson was brave?

choices.label: A
choices.text: He was born in Georgia in 1919

choices.label: B
choices.text: He excelled at four sports in college

choices.label: C
choices.text: He faced terrible discrimination but kept playing

choices.label: D
choices.text: He played in Major League Baseball

items.explanation: The detail that he faced terrible discrimination but kept playing directly shows bravery. The other options are facts about his life but do not directly support the claim about courage.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Clouds form when warm air rises and cools. As the air cools, the water vapor in it condenses around tiny particles of dust or sea salt. Tiny water droplets form around these particles. Millions of droplets together form a visible cloud. Different types of clouds form at different altitudes and temperatures, which is why clouds have different shapes and textures.

What is the main idea of this passage? Which detail is most important for understanding why clouds look different from each other?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Main idea: Clouds are made of water. Most important detail: water vapor condenses around dust particles

choices.label: B
choices.text: Main idea: Clouds form through a process involving rising air, cooling, and condensation. Most important detail: different clouds form at different altitudes and temperatures, explaining their varied shapes

choices.label: C
choices.text: Main idea: Clouds are caused by dust in the air. Most important detail: warm air rises

choices.label: D
choices.text: Main idea: All clouds look the same. Most important detail: millions of droplets form a cloud

items.explanation: The main idea covers the whole formation process, not just one step. The detail about altitude and temperature explains why clouds differ in appearance, which is what the passage's final sentence addresses.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Langston Hughes was born in Joplin, Missouri, in 1902. He moved to Harlem in New York City as a young man and became one of the leading voices of the Harlem Renaissance. He wrote poetry, plays, and stories that celebrated Black American life and culture. His work was influenced by jazz and blues music, and his poems often have a musical rhythm. He wanted his writing to speak directly to working-class Black Americans.

What is the main idea of this biography? Which detail best shows what was unique about Hughes's writing?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Main idea: Hughes moved to New York. Unique detail: he was born in Joplin

choices.label: B
choices.text: Main idea: Hughes was a Harlem Renaissance writer who celebrated Black culture. Unique detail: his poetry was influenced by jazz and blues, giving it a musical rhythm

choices.label: C
choices.text: Main idea: Hughes wrote poetry. Unique detail: he wrote plays and stories too

choices.label: D
choices.text: Main idea: Hughes was born in Missouri. Unique detail: the Harlem Renaissance was in New York

items.explanation: The main idea captures Hughes's significance (leading Harlem Renaissance voice celebrating Black culture). The jazz and blues influence giving his poems a musical rhythm is the most distinctive feature of his writing mentioned in the passage.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Deserts receive very little rainfall, usually less than ten inches per year. Because of this, few plants can survive. The plants that do live in deserts, like cacti, have thick waxy coatings that prevent water loss. Some desert animals are nocturnal, meaning they are only active at night when temperatures are cooler. Others burrow underground to escape the heat of the day.

What text structure does this passage use?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sequence: the passage describes events in time order

choices.label: B
choices.text: Compare-contrast: the passage compares deserts to other environments

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cause-and-effect: the passage explains how low rainfall causes specific plant and animal adaptations

choices.label: D
choices.text: How-to: the passage gives steps for surviving in a desert

items.explanation: The passage begins with low rainfall as the cause and then describes multiple effects: few plants survive, cacti have wax coatings, animals are nocturnal or burrow. The structure is cause-and-effect throughout.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Before the Civil Rights Act of 1964, many public places in the Southern United States were legally segregated, meaning Black and white Americans were required to use separate facilities. In 1960, four Black college students in Greensboro, North Carolina, sat down at a whites-only lunch counter and refused to leave when denied service. News of their sit-in spread, and within weeks, thousands of students across the South were conducting similar peaceful protests. By July 1960, the Greensboro lunch counter was desegregated. The sit-in tactic, though simple, demonstrated that peaceful, organized action could force change.

Identify the text structure. Name two clue words or phrases. Then explain what the last sentence contributes to the main idea.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Structure: sequence. Clue words: 'before' and 'within weeks.' The last sentence is a summary that generalizes the lesson of the specific events described.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Structure: compare-contrast. Clue words: 'before' and 'by July 1960.' The last sentence shows that the sit-ins were more effective than marches.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Structure: cause-and-effect. Clue words: 'before' and 'within weeks.' The last sentence describes a cause that led to the desegregation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Structure: how-to. Clue words: 'in 1960' and 'within weeks.' The last sentence gives a new step in the protest process.

items.explanation: The passage follows a time sequence (before 1964, 1960, within weeks, by July 1960) and the clue words 'before' and 'within weeks' signal this structure. The last sentence summarizes the main idea by drawing a lesson from the specific events: peaceful, organized action can force change. This makes Option A the most accurate choice.

items.prompt:
Read the article below.

Fossil fuels like coal, oil, and natural gas release carbon dioxide when burned. This carbon dioxide traps heat in the atmosphere, causing Earth's average temperature to rise. Rising temperatures melt polar ice, which raises sea levels. Higher sea levels increase flooding in coastal cities. As cities flood, people are displaced, placing pressure on inland communities. Scientists call this sequence a climate feedback loop because each effect becomes a cause of the next problem.

What text structure does the passage use? A student claims that identifying the text structure changes how you read the passage. Is this claim correct? Explain.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Structure: compare-contrast. The student is wrong because text structure does not affect comprehension.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Structure: cause-and-effect. The student is correct because recognizing a chain of causes and effects helps you track how each problem leads to the next and understand the passage as a connected system, not a list of unrelated facts.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Structure: sequence. The student is correct because reading in order is the only way to understand any informational text.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Structure: cause-and-effect. The student is wrong because you only need to read the first and last sentences to understand any informational text.

items.explanation: The passage uses cause-and-effect (each event causes the next, forming a feedback loop). The student's claim is correct: knowing the structure is cause-and-effect helps you actively trace the chain from burning fossil fuels to displaced populations, rather than reading a list of climate facts. Identifying structure shapes how deeply and accurately you understand a complex informational text.
